selector.rationale: Evidence of a pedunculated ureteral tumor with a vulnerable surface and a tubular filling defect with partial obstruction of the right mid ureter supports the diagnosis of a ureteral fibroepithelial polyp, which is a more specific entity than a fibroepithelial polyp.

rejected.label: Inflammatory ureteral stricture
rejected.why: Lack of evidence for inflammation and presence of a tumor-like mass

rejected.label: Ureteral papilloma
rejected.why: Less specific and no direct evidence to support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Ureteral polyp
rejected.why: Less specific than ureteral fibroepithelial polyp

rejected.label: Ureteral tumor
rejected.why: Too broad and does not specify the type of tumor

support_spans: a pedunculated ureteral tumor with a vulnerable surface
Intravenous urography demonstrated a tubular filling defect with partial obstruction of the right mid ureter
Retrograde ureteropyelography confirmed a 5 cm long tubular mass in the mid ureter proximal to the iliac vessels
contradict_spans: Urine cytology and endoscopic biopsy of the lesion and renal pelvis were negative for malignancy
